name: Sleep studies (polysomnography)
summary: How expats arrange overnight sleep studies in Singapore for OSA workups — lab vs home tests, referral paths, and how results feed CPAP or dental-appliance decisions.
body:
A sleep study measures breathing, oxygen, and sleep stages to diagnose obstructive sleep apnoea and related disorders. It sits upstream of CPAP clinics and oral-appliance pathways — do not buy machines or dental devices before the diagnostic question is answered.

## Formats
- In-lab overnight polysomnography (attended)
- Home sleep apnoea testing for selected patients
- Titration studies when CPAP settings need formal calibration
- Multiple sleep latency testing in rarer hypersomnia workups

Your sleep physician or ENT/respiratory referrer chooses the modality; DIY consumer rings are not a substitute for reimbursement-grade diagnosis.

## Access and cost
Public pathways are referral-gated; private sleep labs offer faster booking at higher cash cost. Insurance may cover medically indicated studies with pre-auth — confirm before the night stay. Bring medication lists and note shift-work patterns that affect scheduling.

## How to choose
Prefer labs that explain hookup comfort, cancellation rules, and how quickly scored reports return to the referring doctor. Ask whether a split-night study is possible. Avoid vendors selling CPAP the same morning as an unreviewed home test.

## Practical tip
Skip afternoon caffeine and heavy alcohol before the study unless told otherwise. Pack button-front pyjamas and your usual nasal sprays — wire comfort affects sleep quality and data usefulness.
whenToEngage: Loud snoring / witnessed apnoeas need formal diagnosis
Lab vs home sleep-test modality unclear
CPAP or oral-appliance decision waiting on study results
